producer_report.summary: I added docs/ontology.toml with the seven terms: planning, job, Athena, Hermes, product versus system, landed and Sri. Each has a definition, the misread that caused it, sources and relations. The Hermes entry covers both senses and gives a source for each 'not part of' claim. `cargo test --locked`, clippy with warnings denied, and `cargo fmt --all --check` all pass. The new test crates/athena-cli/tests/ontology.rs parses the file and checks fields, that sources exist (a path, or a decision id with a heading in docs/decisions.md), that relation targets are defined, and that term names are unique. Its in-memory negative tests cover a missing sources field, empty sources, a non-existent source, a dangling relation target, a duplicate term and a bad `not_part_of` source. A second test pins the key wording: both Hermes senses, landed, Sri's pronouns and job id, and Athena not being the whole system. I added decision D109 to docs/decisions.md, a line in docs/architecture.md, and an Added entry in CHANGELOG.md. D109 cites decision 5 of the 2026-10-17 Olympus sheet, lists alternatives (no ontology, per-study glossaries only, a formal ontology) and says the study keeps its own concept model. I wrote none of the banned words, and the xtask vocabulary test passes.

checks_run.note: Whole suite passed, including xtask policy tests and the new ontology tests.
The first, non-quiet run printed output too large to inspect; the -q rerun showed every result ok.

criteria_check.criterion: docs/ontology.toml defines the seven terms (planning, job, Athena, Hermes, product versus system, landed, Sri). Each has a definition, the misread that caused it, a sources field naming existing paths or decision ids, and relations whose targets are all defined terms.
criteria_check.evidence: docs/ontology.toml has seven [[term]] entries. The tests the_ontology_file_is_sound and the_ontology_defines_the_seven_seeded_terms_with_their_meaning pass.

criteria_check.criterion: The Hermes entry names both senses (Hermes Agent, Part 2 S1, not part of Athena; Hermes as Orchestration god in the Olympus Pantheon, BRIEF.md), says which is part of Olympus, and cites a source for each 'not part of' claim.
criteria_check.evidence: The Hermes definition covers both senses and says 'Only this second sense is part of Olympus'. Two not_part_of entries carry sources, and the test checks that they exist.

criteria_check.criterion: Relations match Olympus: the system is Olympus, Athena is the strategy and learning role within it, Sri owns Olympus. No relation makes Athena the whole system.
criteria_check.evidence: Athena has role_within -> product versus system, and its definition says 'not the whole system'. Sri has owns -> product versus system, whose definition names Olympus as the system.

criteria_check.criterion: The file states a term is added only when it causes a misread and how a check reads it (parse path and fields). Landed means merged on main through a verified pull request. The Sri term says use the name or 'they', never he or she, and cites job 20261017-173504-91ys. No per-occurrence BRIEF.md cross-check exists.
criteria_check.evidence: The header comment and [about].rule state the rule and the read path. The test asserts the landed and Sri text. The Sri misread field cites the job id. No test cross-checks BRIEF.md occurrences.

criteria_check.criterion: docs/decisions.md has a new entry keeping the ontology, citing the Olympus 2026-10-17 decision sheet (decision 5), listing alternatives (no ontology; per-study glossaries only), and stating studies keep their own concept model so firstmate, Hermes Agent and Athena are compared in the same terms. docs/decision-links.toml is updated if required and CHANGELOG.md has an entry.
criteria_check.evidence: D109 was appended at the end of docs/decisions.md, so the line numbers in decision-links.toml are unchanged and the file needs no edit. The cargo test run, which includes the backtest tests, passed. CHANGELOG.md has an Added entry.

criteria_check.criterion: Run `cargo test --locked`: the whole suite passes, including the new ontology test on docs/ontology.toml, in-memory negative tests (missing sources field, non-existent source, dangling relation target, duplicate term), and xtask's athena_refers_to_no_one_who_runs_it_or_where. Run `cargo clippy` (clean) and `cargo fmt --check` (passes).
criteria_check.evidence: cargo test --locked -q reported every result ok. clippy with -D warnings is clean. cargo fmt --all --check printed nothing.

criteria_check.criterion: No secrets or personal data, including the user's email address, appear in any new or changed file.
criteria_check.evidence: I wrote none. The new text names only Sri, a job id and paths.

open_issues: I did not edit Cargo.toml, Cargo.lock or docs/design/job-planning.md. The brief lists them as expected deliverables, but nothing in the change needs them.
The Hermes 'not part of Olympus' claim cites docs/design/roadmap.md, which describes Hermes Agent as a studied system. A reviewer may want a more direct source.
mistakes: My first cargo test run, without -q, printed output too large to read, and I could not read the saved file. I reran with -q and checked every result.
learnings: The athena-cli crate already has the toml, serde and tempfile dependencies, so Cargo.toml and Cargo.lock needed no change.
Data files such as TOML need no entry in docs/non-rust-files.md.
A new decision appended at the end of docs/decisions.md does not shift the line numbers recorded in docs/decision-links.toml.
docs/design/job-planning.md contains no banned word at base, and I did not touch it.
desires: Bash could not read a saved tool-output file, because the policy hook blocks paths outside the working directory. A quiet flag on the test command worked around it.
